headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP-enabled coding agent paired with an allowlisted research agent creates default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, so if nuwa-skill consumes shared files or MCP outputs, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pair has a filesystem bridge via Gemini CLI, while nuwa-skill exposes no isolation or parsing safeguards, so the interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP-backed artifact store
IF nuwa-skill parses Gemini CLI output as instructions or task state
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the agents
Route Gemini CLI output through a human-reviewed text file only
Require provenance tags on any MCP-fed content
Run one agent at a time in separate directories
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive files read by Gemini CLI can be forwarded into nuwa-skill’s outputs or remote calls. The profiles do not prove a leak by default, but the shared-file pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or copied artifacts
IF Gemini CLI is given secrets or sensitive source files in cwd
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict Gemini CLI to a scrubbed repo clone
Review outbound requests from nuwa-skill before execution
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. nuwa-skill exposes no locking or coordination primitives, so concurrent writes to the same repo can race and corrupt state. This is a default-dangerous overlap because the write surfaces are explicit on one side and unconstrained on the other.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout
IF nuwa-skill writes or commits to the same repository without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize git writes with a lock file
Disable auto-commit behavior during parallel runs
Use read-only mounts for one agent
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce code and shell actions from files and MCP inputs, while nuwa-skill’s role is scientific-research with allowlisted egress. If nuwa-skill treats Gemini CLI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream remote actions or reports. The profiles do not show verification steps, so the safer assumption is a real but not proven default-path dependency.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes Gemini CLI output without independent verification
IF Gemini CLI output is used as the sole source for a report or action
mitigations: Require a second-pass review before any action
Separate generation from execution roles
Add citation/trace checks on Gemini CLI outputs
Limit nuwa-skill to summarization only
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI explicitly handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment, but the profiles do not identify regulated data classes or residency constraints for nuwa-skill. With only docs-level evidence and no stated mismatch, the compliance risk is limited to documented-policy gaps rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF nuwa-skill is later assigned a residency or retention policy incompatible with Gemini CLI
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace
Document retention expectations for both agents
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
Use separate storage for regulated datasets
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
